This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 (for short "MV Act") has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company being aggrieved by the award dated 12.02.2019 passed in MACT No.102/2018 by the Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to the First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur (CG).

entities.text: First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. By the impugned award, against the claim of Rs. 28,08,000/- made by the respondents No. 1 to 6/claimants, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 12,79,600/-.

The claim application under Section 166 of the MV Act was filed by the respondents No. 1 to 6/claimants inter alia pleading that deceased Ranjeet Singh, met with an accident with the offending vehicle and died on 19.11.2017 by rash and negligent driving of the vehicle Tata Pickup bearing registration No.
CG04-JC0969 driven by respondent No.7/driver owned by respondent No.8/owner and insured with the appellant/Insurance Company.
3. As per the pleadings, the deceased was aged about 30 years and was earning Rs. 15,000/- per month and was working as a mason and the claimants were dependents upon him.
The accident was reported and a criminal case No. 340/2017 under Sections 279,337,338 and 304-A IPC has been registered against the respondent No.7/driver.

The claim application was resisted by the respondent No.7/driver and respondent No.8/owner and the appellant/insurance company on various grounds including the insurance company taking a plea that the driver of the offending Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1735 vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license, the deceased contributed in causing the accident and therefore the Insurance Company may be exonerated.
4. Learned Tribunal framed as many as five issues and decided the same in favour of respondent No.1 to 6/claimants.

5. Shri Sudhir Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company fairly submits that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license, he was holding the license only for driving light motor vehicle and there was no endorsement on the driving license.
Apart from this, he submits that the deceased also contributed in causing the accident therefore some amount may be reduced.
He further submits that opportunity of hearing was not granted.

6. Shri Thakur learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 6/claimants submits that the submission made by the appellant/insurance Company is liable to far fledge as the offending vehicle was a TATA Pickup and its weight was less than 7500 kgs.
and the defence of the Insurance Company is squarely covered with the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs.Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2017) 14 SCC 663.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This apart, he submits that so far as the submission of contributory negligence is concerned, no evidence has been lead by the Insurance company.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the material on record.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1735 8.
The first submission of Shri Agrawal, is squarely covered by the judgment in the matter of Mukund Dewangan (supra).
Hence, it is rejected.

So far as the second submission with regard to contributory negligence is concerned, from perusal of the evidence on record, the learned Tribunal gave a categorical finding that it is the driver of the offending vehicle who was negligent in causing the accident.
The finding so recorded does not appear to be contrary to the evidence and perverse to the record.
The defence of valid and effective driving license has already been considered by the learned Tribunal hence, it cannot be said that no proper opportunity was afforded.
In view of the above, the appeal stands dismissed.

Sd/-
(Sachin Singh Rajput) Judge suguna The New India Insurance Company Limited vs Sunita Bai on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75688063/
